topic: Kingdom Protista: Major Groups and Examples
title: What Swims in Pond Water? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
Diya puts one drop of pond water under the college microscope, and the drop is alive: cells swim, crawl and spin. Red tides in the sea and malaria from a mosquito bite come from the same kind of life: single cells with a true nucleus. These are protists.

A zoom ladder goes from a pond to one drop to Euglena, labelled: long and short flagella, pellicle, nucleus and chloroplasts. Then the five groups run one by one with live animations: chrysophytes (diatom soap box walls, diatomaceous earth), dinoflagellates (cellulose plates, two flagella, red tides of Gonyaulax), euglenoids, slime moulds (plasmodium, fruiting bodies, spores on the air) and the protozoans Amoeba, Trypanosoma, Paramoecium and Plasmodium. Euglena in light vs dark, a pause-and-think check, a worked clue sort, the slime mould exam trap, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 14 of our PUC Biology series.
Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and NEET students.
